sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: headlight distances, restricted lights, bumpers and mirrors, tire pressure sources and tint limits
Confusable pairs among the vehicle equipment rules; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A02
Two different distances apply to headlights: high beams must show objects at least 350 feet ahead, while headlights must be on any time you cannot see the road for at least 500 feet. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlights; confusable high beam reach versus visibility trigger; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A02
Blue lights belong only to snowplows, road maintenance equipment and emergency vehicles, while tow trucks, service vehicles and farm equipment may show flashing lights but not blue ones. [A02]
Why it matters: group restricted lights; confusable blue versus flashing; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A02
School buses may use both flashing lights and strobe lamps, and rural mail carrier vehicles may use strobe lamps but are not on the flashing-light list. [A02]
Why it matters: group restricted lights; confusable flashing versus strobe.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
Daytime running lights can turn on by themselves, but taillights and parking lights never do, so at sunset you still switch on your headlights. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlights; confusable automatic daytime lights versus required headlights.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A01
A private passenger car needs bumpers front and rear, but a pickup or van may use reflectors in place of a rear bumper as long as it has a front bumper. [A01]
Why it matters: group equipment; confusable car versus pickup or van.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A02
Every passenger vehicle needs a rearview mirror, and a hauling pickup or a vehicle with no view through the rear window needs an extra side mirror as well. [A02]
Why it matters: group mirrors; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A03
The tire pressure to aim for is the one on the driver's door sticker or in the owner's manual, while the sidewall number is not the target. [A03]
Why it matters: group tires; confusable door sticker versus sidewall; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A03
Tire pressure is checked either before you drive or only once at least three hours have passed since driving, not right after a trip. [A03]
Why it matters: group tires; prereq for the monthly pressure-loss fact.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A03
The legal tread limit is one-sixteenth of an inch, and the penny test passes only when tread covers part of Lincoln's head. [A03]
Why it matters: group tires; confusable legal limit versus penny test result.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A03
Dark tint that lets through less than 50 percent of light or reflects more than 20 percent is limited to pickup rear windows and to the rear and side windows of vans, limousines and funeral home vehicles, never the windshield. [A03]
Why it matters: group glass; confusable transmit versus reflect limits; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A03
Toll devices and park or inspection stickers allowed by state law may go on the windshield, but objects may not hang between the driver and the windshield. [A03]
Why it matters: group glass; confusable allowed stickers versus hanging objects.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]
